newsitem.title: USA: Neurogen, Pfizer anxiety drug IND filed.
newsitem.headline: Neurogen, Pfizer anxiety drug IND filed.

text.p: Neurogen Corp said Thursday that an Investigational New Drug (IND) application has been filed with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to begin human clinical testing of a drug to relieve anxiety.
The IND was filed by Pfizer Inc for NGD 91-2, a non-sedating GABA receptor subtype-specific drug.
Neurogen and Pfizer are collaborating to develop drugs to treat anxiety, sleep disorders and cognition enhancement through the GABA neurotransmitter system.
The Phase I clinical trials on the drug's safety and pharmacological action will be conducted by Pfizer and are planned for this summer.

Neurogen said that a related drug, NGD 91-1, eased anxiety in human clinical trials with a single dose of small molecule drug to the same extent as a 10 mg dose of Valium, without the sedation associated with Valium. NGD 91-1, like NGD 91-2, acts on a specific set of GABA receptor subtypes.

"Like NGD 91-1, the newer candidate, NGD 91-2, demonstrates in animal studies efficacy in reducing anxiety without causing side effects, such as sedation, while exhibiting pharmacokinetics superior to NGD 91-1," said Harry Penner, Neurogen President and chief executive officer in a press release.
Valium is made by Roche Products.
